findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass the password when any totpCode is sent
findings.body: The new branch accepts `credentials.backupCode` as sufficient to validate the second factor, but the password check above only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`. A request with a valid backup code plus any non-empty dummy `totpCode` therefore skips password verification and logs in using only the backup code. Since backup codes are often printed or exported, this defeats the password factor. Password verification must also be required when `credentials.backupCode` is present, or the TOTP-only bypass must be scoped to the trusted `totp` flow.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read/modify/write
findings.body: The code decrypts the whole backup-code list, mutates one element to null, and writes the whole encrypted list back. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the original array and both succeed, violating single-use. Two concurrent logins with different codes can each null a different index, and the last write wins, resurrecting the other already-used code. Use a DB transaction/conditional update or a row per code so consumption is atomic.

findings.title: Backup-code recovery is unreachable for `?totp=` logins
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is present (the `/auth/login?totp=...` flow used after OAuth/SAML sign-in), `footerText` renders `ExternalTotpFooter`, which only has Cancel. The new Lost access button that sets `twoFactorLostAccess` exists only in `TwoFactorFooter`, so the `BackupCode` form can never be shown. A 2FA-enabled user who reaches login through this path cannot use their backup codes if the authenticator is lost.

findings.title: onEnable is skipped if the backup-code dialog is dismissed via Escape/outside click
findings.body: After `handleEnable` succeeds, 2FA is already enabled server-side and the modal switches to DisplayBackupCodes, but `onEnable()` is only called by the Close button at line 269. The `Dialog` still receives the parent's `onOpenChange`, so pressing Escape or clicking outside closes it without notifying the parent or resetting state. The settings page can remain showing 2FA as disabled, and the user may not have saved the codes. Handle `onOpenChange` or call `onEnable` when entering the backup-code step.

findings.title: Core backup-code login/disable paths are untested
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only verifies that the backup-code screen appears and that download/copy/close controls work. It never submits a backup code to `next-auth-options` or the disable endpoint, so the new password/backup-code logic (including the password-bypass and single-use behavior above) is not exercised. Add tests for successful backup-code login, rejection/reuse of a consumed code, and disabling 2FA with a backup code.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button makes it unreachable by keyboard for every PasswordField in the app. Keyboard-only users can no longer toggle password visibility; this is an accessibility regression unrelated to the 2FA feature. Remove the tabIndex or provide an accessible alternative.
